class.name: PhysXWaterfalls3D
class.brief_description: Contact waterfalls: water that stays on steep rock, from a terrain's waterfall records.
class.description: Reads [code]get_waterfalls()[/code] from [member source] (a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code], or any node returning the same records: [code]type[/code], [code]top[/code], [code]bottom[/code], [code]height[/code], [code]discharge[/code], [code]direction[/code], [code]lip_points[/code], [code]lip_share[/code], [code]lip_width[/code], [code]face_profiles[/code], [code]ledges[/code]) and drapes a sheet of water down every fall that is not a free plunge (cascades, horsetails and tiered falls). The sheet covers the wet part of the lip and follows the ground under each column (the source's [code]get_height()[/code] every 0.5 m, else the record's three face profiles smoothed with a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline). Down each column: speed from gravity against Darcy-Weisbach friction ([member friction_factor]) on the depth, so the sheet nears the normal speed [code](8 g q sin a / f)^(1/3)[/code] of chute flow (Chanson 1993) and slows on the foot; no air above the inception point (Wood, Ackers and Loveless 1983, [method inception_length]) and air towards [method equilibrium_air] below it; thickness bulked by the air. Clear water at the lip, white below, with streaks carried at the water's speed. Spray at each ledge and at the foot, and a [PhysXWaterMist3D] along the face for falls carrying at least [member mist_min_discharge]. Every [PhysXRiver3D] in the tree is told about these faces ([member PhysXRiver3D.fall_exclusions]), so it does not draw them again as free jets.

method.name: equilibrium_air
method.description: The mean air concentration self-aerated flow reaches on a chute of this slope, [code]0.9 sin a[/code] (Chanson 1993), at most 0.9.

method.name: get_contact_shader_code
method.description: The shader the sheets are drawn with: water that fades in over its wandering edge, wet rock in patches past it, white water with streaks below the inception point.

method.name: get_contact_falls
method.description: One dictionary per contact fall drawn: [code]id[/code], [code]type[/code], [code]height[/code], [code]discharge[/code] (m³/s), [code]inception_length[/code] (m from the lip), [code]air_at_foot[/code], [code]air_peak[/code], [code]impact_speed[/code] (m/s at the foot), [code]ledges[/code] and [code]rows[/code].

method.name: inception_length
method.description: Distance (m) from the lip to the inception point of self-aeration on a chute: [code]L_i / k_s = 13.6 (sin a)^0.0796 F*^0.713[/code] with [code]F* = q / sqrt(g sin a k_s³)[/code], for discharge [param q] per metre of width (m²/s) and roughness height [param ks] (m).

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Reads the source's records again and rebuilds the sheets, spray and mist.

members.member: Draws the contact falls. Off, the node draws nothing and the rivers draw their falls as before.
Darcy-Weisbach friction factor of white water on the rock face (about 0.1 to 0.3 on rough or stepped rock). Higher is slower, thicker water.
Falls lower than this (m) are left to the rivers.
A [PhysXWaterMist3D] along each face that carries at least [member mist_min_discharge].
Scales the mist each face throws.
Faces carrying less water (m³/s) throw no mist: a trickle wets the rock but makes no measurable mist.
Roughness height of the rock face (m), for the inception point.
Distance (m) between rows of the sheet down the face.
The node whose [code]get_waterfalls()[/code] lists the falls.
Spray at each ledge and at the foot of each face.
Width (m) of wet rock drawn either side of the water: darker and glossy, in patches.
